sentences.text: Hovacrex was a large gallinule, a type of rail, that lived exclusively on the island of Madagascar. Its body size was roughly comparable to that of the modern Tasmanian nativehen.
This bird survived during the Late Pleistocene, with fossils dating from 0.129 to 0.0117 million years ago.
Andrews first described the species in 1897 under the name Tribonyx roberti.
Brodkorb later established the distinct genus Hovacrex in 1965.
It remains uncertain whether the species was flightless, as fossils from Sirabé in central Madagascar lack wing bones.
The animal belongs to the rail family, Rallidae, and was originally placed in the genus Tribonyx.
Some researchers suggest it may be synonymous with the genus Gallinula.
